subject: Sequenced latency commitments and short-burst carveout discussion
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@stratifylabs.com>
To: ben.carter@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@stratifylabs.com
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API latency commitments — onboarding phasing and short-burst carveouts

Hi Ben,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Stratify is excited about Redwood’s hosted API, but procurement and engineering flagged two concerns we need clarified before we proceed:

1) Precise latency SLOs during onboarding — we understand you offer p50/p95 windows, but we need a phased commitment for the first 90 days while we ramp traffic and tune prompts.
2) Short-burst behavior — during our nightly batch-to-realtime migration (large bursts for 7–10 minutes), we expect transient tail degradation. We need to understand how Redwood measures p95, whether there’s a carveout for short bursts, and what operational mitigations you offer.

Can you share a proposed phased SLO plan (initial probation, steady-state, and post-tuning targets), the measurement windowing approach, and any temporary relief mechanics (credits or fallback routing) you’d contractually accept? Also, please attach any evidence you can share on similar customers.

We’d like to schedule a 30-minute call this week to align.

Best,
Alex
Director of Engineering, Stratify Labs

Subject: Re: Hosted API latency commitments — onboarding phasing and short-burst carveouts

Alex — thanks for the clear asks. I attached a short draft (stratify-slo-draft-v1.pdf) that outlines a sequenced commitment approach and a short evidence CSV from a similar onboarding. High-level proposal below; happy to go into details on the call.

Proposed sequenced commitments (hosted API):
- Phase 0 (Onboarding probation, first 14 days): p50 <= 120ms, p95 <= 420ms measured as rolling 5-minute percentiles sampled every 1 minute (to reflect immediate bursts while we warm caches).
- Phase 1 (Ramp, days 15–45): p50 <= 95ms, p95 <= 350ms measured as 5-minute rolling percentiles aggregated into hourly windows for SLA reporting.
- Phase 2 (Steady-state, day 46+): p50 <= 85ms, p95 <= 320ms with full SLA enforcement on hourly aggregated windows.

Measurement details and carveouts:
- Measurement: We compute p50/p95 from per-request latencies (server-side end-to-end) using a rolling 5-minute percentile that is sampled every minute. For contractual SLA breaches we aggregate those minute-samples into an hourly measurement window (hourly aggregated p95).
- Short-burst carveout: we propose a temporary short-burst carveout for events where >200x baseline QPS sustained for <= 15 minutes. These events will be cataloged as "short-burst transients" and excluded from SLA breach calculations if (a) customer provides a 24-hour notice for planned migrations, or (b) event is documented and validated by Redwood tracing within 72 hours for unplanned bursts.
- Operational mitigations: auto-fallback to a compatible lower-throughput model variant, prioritized KV cache warm-up, and optional burst-dedicated capacity for the migration window.

Compensation for breaches during the probation period: we typically provide service credits on a pro-rata basis for confirmed breaches during Phase 0; for Phase 1+ standard SLA credit table applies.

Next steps I propose:
- Quick alignment call (30min) today or tomorrow to confirm windows and carveout thresholds.
- We’ll exchange a short evidence package (I attached latency-evidence-202704.csv) and a mutual action plan (we can turn the PDF into a HubSpot task).

I’m available 11:00–12:30 and 15:00–16:30 PT today.

Thanks,
Ben
Enterprise Solutions, Redwood Inference

Ben / Laura — thanks for the quick proposal. A few clarifying points from Stratify engineering and procurement:

- The phased numeric targets look sensible, but procurement needs the short-burst carveout clearly codified: we can accept a <=15 minute carveout for planned migrations, but we want a maximum of two such carveouts per quarter without penalty. Any additional short-burst events should trigger a defined remediation plan and, if repeated, credits.
- For measurement: is Redwood willing to share the raw minute-sample logs (anonymized) for the first 45 days to validate the rollups? We will want to run our own sampling scripts against those logs.
- On fallback models: can you confirm how model-variant fallback interacts with quality? We’d like a guarantee that fallback will not change API response schema and that we can optionally disable fallback if quality is more important than latency for certain routes.

Procurement asks that we include an explicit clause for a temporary "migration relief" that specifies notice periods, per-quarter allowances, and the evidence validation window. We can draft language and send back a redline.

I’ve attached a short list of questions procurement will include in the contract redline; we can cover these on the alignment call.

Regards,
Alex

Alex — thanks, good points. Quick operational commitments from Redwood:

1) Evidence sharing: Redwood will provide anonymized minute-sample CSVs for the first 45 days (same format as attached) and a secure link to trace IDs for validated incidents. We’ll redact any PII.
2) Short-burst policy: we accept the two-per-quarter planned carveout limit; additional events will be remediated per the contract and eligible for SLA credits if the event is caused by platform-side routing or misconfiguration. Unplanned customer-originated bursts (traffic you control) are excluded from credit eligibility.
3) Fallback model behavior: fallback will preserve response schema. We’ll document the quality delta for each fallback variant in the onboarding runbook; you can opt out of automatic fallback on any route, but we’ll require an explicit config flag per-route.

Operational next steps:
- Ben will own drafting the short addendum language for the migration relief clause.
- We’ll set up a shared Drive folder (link sent) and schedule a call Wednesday 10:00 PT to finalize wording and the mutual action plan.

If that works, Ben — please circulate the 1-page addendum and a proposed timeline for the three phases by EOD.

Thanks,
Laura
Head of GTM Contracts, Redwood Inference
